sample_fields.Front:
[[Core Idea::Active recall means retrieving information from memory, not re-reading notes.]]
((Hint::Think of the last time you explained a topic without looking at your notes.))
[Active recall]^(Retrieval strengthens memory traces and improves long-term retention.)
Memory improves with {{retrieval practice}}, not just {{passive review}}.
[
A. Re-read highlighted notes repeatedly
B. Watch summary videos at 2x speed
C. Close your notes and write key points from memory
D. Cram everything in one session
]::(C)
sample_fields.Back:
Correct answer: C.
Explanation: Retrieval practice exposes weak spots and improves long-term retention.

sample_fields.Front:
[[Forgetting Curve::Forgetting is fastest right after learning, then slows down.]]
Convert input into output: {{retrieval practice}} + {{spaced repetition}}.
((Hint::Recall three key terms before revealing the explanation.))
[
A. Six reviews in one day
B. Same-time review with no feedback
C. Gradually expand review intervals based on forgetting
D. Only review the night before exam
]::(C)
sample_fields.Back:
Key line: durable learning comes from effortful recall.
{{retrieval practice}} activates memory; {{spaced repetition}} reinforces it at the right time.
